content.intro: This lesson studies The <TransitionGroup> Component within Styling, Transitions, and Animations. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Useful motion and visual feedback should clarify state changes without reducing readability or accessibility.

content_blocks.title: The <TransitionGroup> Component: Component communication
content_blocks.alt_text: Component communication diagram for lesson 64: The <TransitionGroup> Component. Parent owns the value or business intent → Child receives data and renders its view → Child emits intent; parent decides updates
content_blocks.caption: Component flow: data moves into children through props; emitted events communicate requested changes back to the owner.

items.title: List transition classes
items.text: For List transition classes, keep the visual rule in CSS where possible and bind reactive values only when state genuinely changes presentation. Check responsive behavior and reduced-motion preferences; animation should communicate state rather than block interaction.

items.title: Handling keyed lists
items.text: For Handling keyed lists, express the intended DOM result through a Vue template binding instead of directly manipulating the DOM. Keep template expressions small, use stable keys for stateful list items, and choose directives based on whether content should be created, removed, or merely hidden.
